simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-02.title: Gears alternate
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-02.body:
Two gears that mesh turn in opposite directions. Along the chain A–B–C–D–E–F the directions alternate:

A anti-clockwise, B clockwise, C anti-clockwise, D clockwise, E anti-clockwise, F clockwise.

- A and C turn the same way, so A is false.
- Only 3 gears turn each way, so B is false.
- E turns anti-clockwise, so C is false.
- C turns anti-clockwise, so **D is true**.

**Answer: (D)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-02.title: Odd and even positions
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-02.body:
Gears in odd positions (A, C, E) turn like A, anti-clockwise; gears in even positions (B, D, F) turn clockwise. C is in an odd position, so it turns anti-clockwise.

**Answer: (D)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-03.title: Count in blocks
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-03.body:
There are 5 one-digit numbers (1, 3, 5, 7, 9).

Two-digit numbers: 5 choices for each digit, $5 \times 5 = 25$. So far $5 + 25 = 30$ numbers, the 30th being 99.

Three-digit numbers starting with 1: 111–119 (5 numbers), 131–139, 151–159, 171–179, 191–199 — that is $5 \times 5 = 25$ numbers, numbers 31 to 55.

So the 55th number is the last of them, 199.

**Answer: (D) 199**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-03.title: Base-5 idea
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-03.body:
The odd digits 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 behave like the five digits of a counting system. After the 30 numbers with one or two digits, the next 25 all start with 1, ending at 199. $30 + 25 = 55$.

**Answer: (D) 199**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-04.title: Find the range
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-04.body:
The result must be at most 9999, so the number is at most $9999 - 2020 = 7979$. The smallest four-digit number is 1000.

From 1000 to 7979 there are $7979 - 1000 + 1 = 6980$ numbers.

**Answer: (C) 6980**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-04.title: Count the ones that fail
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-04.body:
There are 9000 four-digit numbers (1000–9999). Those from 7980 to 9999 become five-digit numbers: $9999 - 7980 + 1 = 2020$ of them. $9000 - 2020 = 6980$.

**Answer: (C) 6980**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-05.title: Count how often each number is used
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-05.body:
The grid has the top row 10, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19 and the left column 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. There are 5 columns and 4 rows of empty cells.

Each top number 11, 13, 15, 17, 19 is used in its own cell and in 4 sums: 5 times. Each left number 12, 14, 16, 18 is used in its own cell and in 5 sums: 6 times. The corner 10 is used once.

Sum $= 10 + 5 \times (11 + 13 + 15 + 17 + 19) + 6 \times (12 + 14 + 16 + 18) = 10 + 5 \times 75 + 6 \times 60 = 10 + 375 + 360 = 745$.

**Answer: (A) 745**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-06.title: Digit groups
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-06.body:
Three digits with product 24: $\{1,3,8\}$, $\{1,4,6\}$, $\{2,3,4\}$ (all different: 6 orders each) and $\{2,2,6\}$ (3 orders). Total $6 + 6 + 6 + 3 = 21$.

**Answer: (E)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-07.title: The last day
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-07.body:
December has 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 days, so exactly three weekdays occur 5 times: the weekdays of December 1, 2 and 3.

Saturday occurs 5 times but Sunday only 4 times, so Saturday must be the last of those three days: December 3 is a Saturday. Then December 1 is a **Thursday**.

**Answer: (D) Thursday**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-07.title: Go backwards from the 31st
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-07.body:
If there is no fifth Sunday after the fifth Saturday, the fifth Saturday is December 31. Going back 28 days, December 3 is also a Saturday, so December 1 is a Thursday.

**Answer: (D) Thursday**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-08.title: Sides minus number, squared
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-08.body:
Each number sits in a shape. Take (number of sides of the shape − the number) and square it:

- Square (4 sides), 1: $(4 - 1)^2 = 9$ ✓
- Hexagon (6 sides), 2: $(6 - 2)^2 = 16$ ✓
- Octagon (8 sides), 6: $(8 - 6)^2 = 4$ ✓
- Pentagon (5 sides), 1: $(5 - 1)^2 = 16$

**Answer: (C) 16**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-08.title: Check the other choices
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-08.body:
The answers 9, 16, 4 are all square numbers, so the missing value is probably a square too — among the choices only 16 is a square. The rule above confirms it.

**Answer: (C) 16**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-09.title: Change to thirds
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-09.body:
Write each number in thirds: $6\frac{1}{3} = \frac{19}{3}$, $7 = \frac{21}{3}$, $7\frac{2}{3} = \frac{23}{3}$, …, $31 = \frac{93}{3}$.

So we count the odd numbers 19, 21, 23, …, 93: $(93 - 19) \div 2 + 1 = 38$.

**Answer: (C) 38**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-09.title: Count steps
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-09.body:
Each step adds $\frac{2}{3}$. From $6\frac{1}{3}$ to $31$ is $24\frac{2}{3} = \frac{74}{3}$, which is $74 \div 2 = 37$ steps. 37 steps means 38 numbers.

**Answer: (C) 38**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-10.title: Digit sum rule
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-10.body:
A number is a multiple of 9 when its digit sum is. $2 + 5 + M + 4 + 8 = 19 + M$. The next multiple of 9 after 19 is 27, so $M = 8$ (36 would need $M = 17$, not a digit).

**Answer: (B) 8**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-11.title: Half of each strip
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-11.body:
Each rectangle is cut into horizontal (ABCD) or vertical (PQRS) strips. Inside every strip, the shaded triangles and the white triangles have bases along the same lines and the same height, so the shaded part is exactly half of that strip.

So in both rectangles the shaded area is half of $10 \times 6 = 60$ cm², i.e. 30 cm². They are equal.

**Answer: (A)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-11.title: Triangle area rule
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-11.body:
A triangle whose base lies on one side of a strip and whose top vertex is on the opposite side has area $\frac{1}{2} \times$ base $\times$ strip height. In each strip the shaded triangles' bases add up to the full strip width, so the shaded area is $\frac{1}{2} \times$ strip area. Adding the strips: half of each rectangle, 30 cm² each.

**Answer: (A)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-12.title: Find the next such time
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-12.body:
After 4:56 the next candidates would be 5:67, 6:78, 7:89 — not real times. The next one is **12:34** A.M. (digits 1, 2, 3, 4).

From 4:56 P.M. to 12:34 A.M.: 4:56 P.M. → 11:56 P.M. is 7 hours; 11:56 P.M. → 12:34 A.M. is 38 minutes. Total $7 \times 60 + 38 = 458$ minutes.

**Answer: (B) 458 minutes**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-12.title: Using 24-hour time
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-12.body:
12:34 A.M. is 00:34. From 16:56 to 24:00 is $7$ h $4$ min $= 424$ minutes; then 34 more minutes: $424 + 34 = 458$.

**Answer: (B) 458 minutes**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-13.title: Follow the wax
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-13.body:
- 80 candles last 80 days and leave 80 pieces of wax → 20 new candles.
- 20 candles last 20 days → 20 pieces of wax → 5 new candles.
- 5 candles last 5 days → 5 pieces of wax → 1 new candle (1 piece left over).
- 1 candle lasts 1 day → now 2 pieces of wax, not enough for another candle.

Total $80 + 20 + 5 + 1 = 106$ days, which is not among A–D.

**Answer: (E) None of the above** (106 days)

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-14.title: Test each person
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-14.body:
- If George watched it: George lies, Helen and Irene tell the truth → only 1 liar ✗
- If Helen watched it: George tells the truth, Helen lies, Irene tells the truth → 1 liar ✗
- If Irene watched it: George lies, Helen tells the truth, Irene lies → 2 liars ✓

**Answer: (C) Irene**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-14.title: George and Helen disagree
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-14.body:
George and Helen say opposite things, so exactly one of them lies. Since two people lied, Irene must be the other liar — so Irene did watch it.

**Answer: (C) Irene**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-15.title: Match the three faces
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-15.body:
The missing corner piece shows three faces of the big cube: a top face, a left face and a right face. Look at the pattern on the big cube around the hole: each of those faces must continue the dark/light triangles on the surrounding parts of the big cube.

Only options B and E show all three correct face patterns, and of these only B has them in the right orientation (E has the patterns turned).

**Answer: (B)**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-17.title: Count by size
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-17.body:
Count the triangles by how many small regions they are made of:

- 1-part: 11
- 2-part: 12
- 3-part: 6
- 4-part: 6
- 5-part: 3
- 7-part: 4

Total $11 + 12 + 6 + 6 + 3 + 4 = 42$.

**Answer: 42**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-17.title: Choose three lines
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-17.body:
A triangle is formed by three of the drawn lines that meet in three different points (on the drawn segments). There are 9 lines: the two sides, the bottom, and six slanted lines, several of which pass through the same central point. Going through all choices of three lines carefully (for example by computer) and leaving out triples that meet in a single point or do not meet on the segments gives 42 triangles.

**Answer: 42**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-18.title: Work backwards
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-18.body:
Undo each step in reverse order:

- $80 \times 8 = 640$
- $640 + 8 = 648$
- $648 \div 8 = 81$
- $81 - 8 = 73$

**Answer: 73**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-19.title: Count units
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-19.body:
Let the gap between two lines be 1 unit. Jan 2, Feb 4, Mar 5, Apr 3, May 1, Jun 5 units.

Jan + May = 3 units, June = 5 units, so 2 units = 200 guests and 1 unit = 100 guests.

Total: $2 + 4 + 5 + 3 + 1 + 5 = 20$ units $= 2000$ guests.

**Answer: 2000**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-20.title: Count the sides
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-20.body:
Let the square have side $s$. The top two rectangles together have widths adding to $s$ and each has the top part's height; the same for the bottom two.

Top pair: perimeters $2(a + h) + 2(s - a + h) = 2s + 4h$. Bottom pair: $2s + 4(s - h)$. Total $= 2s + 4h + 2s + 4s - 4h = 8s$.

$8s = 72$, so $s = 9$ cm.

**Answer: 9**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-20.title: Think of lengths
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-20.body:
Every horizontal length in the four perimeters adds up to the side of the square four times (top and bottom of the top row, top and bottom of the bottom row), and every vertical length also adds up to the side four times. So the sum of the perimeters is $8 \times$ side $= 72$, side $= 9$.

**Answer: 9**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-21.title: Colour it with two
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-21.body:
One colour is not enough (connected circles must differ). Try 2 colours, yellow (Y) and green (G): colour the outer square Y, G, Y, G going round, and each inner circle the opposite colour of the outer circle it is joined to. Then the inner square also alternates G, Y, G, Y, and every segment joins a Y and a G.

So 2 colours suffice.

**Answer: 2**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-21.title: Like a chessboard
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-21.body:
The figure is a cube drawn flat. Think of the corners of a cube as having coordinates of 0s and 1s; colour a corner by whether it has an even or odd number of 1s. Every edge changes exactly one coordinate, so it joins different colours. Two colours work, and one does not.

**Answer: 2**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-22.title: Units
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-22.body:
Let the cows be 3 units. Then $3 \times$ chickens $= 5 \times 3$ units, so chickens = 5 units. And $2 \times$ goats $= 10 \times 3$ units, so goats = 15 units.

Chickens + goats $= 20$ units $= 40$, so 1 unit $= 2$: 10 chickens, 30 goats, 6 cows.

Feet: $10 \times 2 + 30 \times 4 + 6 \times 4 = 20 + 120 + 24 = 164$.

**Answer: 164**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-22.title: Compare with the cows
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-22.body:
Goats = 5 × cows and chickens = $\frac{5}{3}$ × cows. So cows must be a multiple of 3. Try cows = 3: chickens 5, goats 15, total 20 — half of 40. So double: cows 6, chickens 10, goats 30. Feet $= 20 + 120 + 24 = 164$.

**Answer: 164**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-23.title: Model method
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-23.body:
Let the candy be 3 units. She ate 1 unit, so 2 units went to school.

At school: $7 \times 26 + 22 = 182 + 22 = 204$ pieces = 2 units, so 1 unit = 102.

She bought $3 \times 102 = 306$ pieces.

**Answer: 306**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-24.title: Count digits by page group
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-24.body:
Pages 1–9: 9 digits. Pages 10–99: $90 \times 2 = 180$ digits. Together 189.

$237 - 189 = 48$ digits are left for 3-digit pages: $48 \div 3 = 16$ pages, i.e. pages 100 to 115.

**Answer: 115**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-25.title: Column by column
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-25.body:
Two 4-digit numbers add to less than 20000, so $A = 1$.

Ones: $C + C$ ends in C, so $C = 0$.

Thousands: $A + D$ (+ carry) gives $10 + C = 10$, so $1 + D + \text{carry} = 10$: $D = 9$ (carry 0) or $D = 8$ (carry 1).

Tens: $A + E = 1 + E$ ends in D (no carry from the ones). If $D = 8$, then $E = 7$, and the hundreds $B + B$ would have to end in $E = 7$ — impossible, $B + B$ is even. So $D = 9$, $E = 8$.

Hundreds: $B + B$ ends in $E = 8$ with no carry out, so $B = 4$.

Check: $1410 + 9480 = 10890$ ✓. So DBEC = 9480.

**Answer: 9480**

simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-25.title: Computer check
simcc-sasmo-2020-g4-25.body:
Trying every assignment of different digits to A, B, C, D, E gives only $1410 + 9480 = 10890$.

**Answer: 9480**
